title: Minimum Seconds to Equalize a Circular Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed array nums containing n integers, at each second, every element is simultaneously replaced with either itself or one of its neighboring elements.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array nums containing n integers, at each second, every element is simultaneously replaced with either itself or one of its neighboring elements. Replace nums[i] with either nums[i], nums[(i - 1 + n) % n], or nums[(i + 1) % n]. Determine the minimum number of seconds needed to make all elements in the array nums equal.
constraints: Each second, every circular-array position may keep its value or copy either neighbor’s value, simultaneously.
Return the minimum seconds needed to make all positions equal.
The final common value must be one already present initially.
hints: Consider each distinct initial value as the final target.
Its occurrences spread outward simultaneously; the slowest region is the largest circular gap between consecutive sources.
Append the first index plus n to represent the wraparound occurrence, then halve the largest gap.
Every position adopts the target from its nearest source, and the midpoint of the largest source gap is exactly the last position reached.
editorial: Every position adopts the target from its nearest source, and the midpoint of the largest source gap is exactly the last position reached.

tests.explanation: Either value spreads one step to cover the alternating circle, so one second is enough.
Value one reaches both middle positions in one second.
